Fig 2: Source code showing no_log=True on input (line 105) vs unprotected output (line 127)

A flaw was found in the community.general Ansible collection's nexmo module.
The module constructs HTTP requests to the Vonage/Nexmo SMS API by encoding
API credentials (api_key and api_secret) into URL query parameters and
sending them via GET requests. This causes credentials to be exposed in web
server access logs, proxy logs, HTTP Referer headers, and network monitoring
tools, despite the Ansible argument specification marking these parameters
as no_log. An attacker with access to any of these logging or monitoring
points can obtain the full API credentials and gain unauthorized access to
the victim's Vonage/Nexmo account.
Server-side request forgery in Azure Machine Learning allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Improper access control in Azure Site Recovery allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5 in the berval2tl_data() function in plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c. The function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2) without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated to uint16_t, yielding 0xFFFE (65534) or 0xFFFF (65535). The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to 65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap out-of-bounds read.
The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or kadmind reads principal data.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 kernel builds. An incomplete backport of the CVE-2026-46099 fix in RHEL 9.6 through 9.10 left a local_bh imbalance in seg6_input_core(), where the drop path returns with bottom halves still disabled. This can lead to softirq starvation and denial of service on systems with SRv6 tunnels configured. Upstream and RHEL 10 are not affected.

An Apache-proxied Dogtag CA REST endpoint exposed by IdM (POST /ca/rest/certrequests) returns HTTP 500 with internal Java stack traces for unauthenticated malformed requests. The same unauthenticated error path emits large multi-line stack traces into the CA debug log, creating a log-amplification resource exhaustion vector (disk growth and I/O contention) without requiring authentication.

Farmasimplex retrieves a CIP News file over HTTP and executes embedded SQL statements against the local FarmaCIP database with administrative privileges. An attacker able to tamper with network communications or compromise vendor infrastructure can inject arbitrary SQL commands, leading to unauthorized access to, modification or deletion of database contents and potentially operating system command execution.

A heap buffer overflow flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. When serializing objectclass definitions, the oc_superior (SUP) field length is omitted from buffer size calculations in read_schema_dse() and schema_oc_to_string(), but the field is still written via strcat(). An attacker with Directory Manager privileges, or a compromised replication supplier, can trigger a server crash by creating objectclasses with long SUP values. This is an incomplete fix variant of CVE-2025-14905.
A logical flaw vulnerability exists in the ZTE Nubia RedMagic 9S Pro+. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may compromise confidentiality.

Z80 Ultra is affected by an information disclosure vulnerability in service interfaces related to application scenarios. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may result in an impact on confidentiality.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability in the game assistant module. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality and integrity.
ZTE Z80 Ultra is affected by an unauthorized access vulnerability. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could result in an impact on integrity.
ZTE Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability in the UI module. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper modification control vulnerability. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect integrity and availability.

An rsync server can send diagnostic data to the client which is mirrored to stdout and collected by Routinator line by line. If an excessive amount of data is sent without a line break, Routinator will eventually run out of memory and crash.

When rejecting a publication point midway during processing amd falling back to the stored version of the publication point, Routinator will keep the data it had processed for the publication point so far rather than dropping it.

The WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary directory deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the singleDeleteCache function in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires either the Custom Permalinks plugin or the GeoDirectory plugin to be co-installed, as these provide the necessary mechanism to write a traversal-bearing permalink value into the database that WP Fastest Cache then consumes without validation.

The PublishPress Capabilities: User Role Access Control, Admin Area Permissions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'page_elements' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.53.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to open a Profile Features capture window and save at least one of the attacker-supplied rows on the Profile Features screen, which represents the ordinary documented use of the feature and leaves no visible indication to the administrator that malicious data was submitted.

Incorrect default permissions in the ASUS DisplayWidget Center allow a local, low-privileged user to achieve arbitrary code execution in the security context of another user via a crafted executable placed in that user-writable directory, which the application launches when the other user runs it and uses a particular feature.Refer to the '
Security Update for ASUS Display Widget Center ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

Authorization bypass through User-Controlled key vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs.

This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command ('SQL injection') vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows SQL Injection.

This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

The Salon Booking System – Appointment Booking for Salons, Barbershops & Spas plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 10.31.16. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite arbitrary users' user meta fields, including the _sln_phone and _sln_sms_prefix meta of administrator accounts, and create bookings attributed to arbitrary users. This is exploitable on default installations because reCAPTCHA is disabled by default, causing the booking endpoint's permission check to return true for any authenticated user without a meaningful authorization gate.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-bad H.265 video parser. When parsing a specially crafted H.265 bitstream containing a Screen Content Coding (SCC) extension with certain palette predictor initializer settings, an integer underflow in the upper-bound computation allows the parser to accept an out-of-range value for the number of palette predictor entries. This causes the parser to write beyond the end of a fixed-size array, resulting in memory corruption and an application crash. An attacker can deliver the malformed bitstream as a local file or over a network stream such as HTTP, HLS, DASH, RTSP, RTP, or WebRTC. Successful exploitation requires the application to open or play that content, and is limited to a denial-of-service impact.

A flaw was found in the H.264 video parser in gst-plugins-bad. When processing a specially crafted H.264 video file or network stream with malformed Multiview (MVC) Sequence Parameter Set data, the parser can dereference a NULL pointer during the cleanup of partially allocated internal structures after a parse failure. This can cause the application using GStreamer to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in GStreamer. An integer overflow vulnerability in the AV1 LEB128 variable-length integer parser allows a remote attacker to cause a crash in applications that process AV1 media content. By crafting a malformed AV1 bitstream containing an invalid LEB128-encoded value, an attacker can cause integer overflow in the parser, resulting in incorrect length values being used during stream processing, which can lead to a denial of service.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-base MicroDVD subtitle parser. When processing a specially crafted subtitle file, the parser may dereference a NULL pointer, causing the application to crash when a user opens or plays media with a malformed MicroDVD (.sub) subtitle file.

An improper neutralization of argument delimiters in a command vulnerability in the OAuth API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.1.1-42962-10, 7.2.1-69057-14, 7.2.2-72806-11, 7.3.2-86009-6, and 7.4.1-90080-2 allows remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and conduct denial-of-service attacks.

A flaw was found in flightctl. A TLS handshake is performed synchronously in the HTTP server’s connection-context callback without a deadline. A network-reachable unauthenticated client can stall the handshake and prevent the affected listener from accepting new connections.

The ShortPixel Image Optimizer – Optimize Images, Convert WebP & AVIF plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the administrator to have enabled the 'Deliver WebP/AVIF images using the ShortPixel CDN' (useCDN) option, after which any unauthenticated visitor can submit a comment containing a crafted url() payload inside an allowed HTML construct such as <acronym title="...">, which WordPress comment kses preserves on save; the dangerous attribute-boundary breakout occurs only at render time inside the ob_start output-buffer rewriter, where kses does not apply.

The Organize Media Folder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'EXIF.DateTimeOriginal' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.00 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This bypass of wp_filter_post_kses means the injected payload survives regardless of the uploader's unfiltered_html capability; Subscriber-level access becomes sufficient when a front-end attachment-upload integration such as bbPress with forumAttachments is active, and exploitation requires no special configuration because the %created_timestamp% placeholder is included in the caption template by default. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that bbPress and gd-bbpress-attachments (forumAttachments) are installed and configured so that Subscribers/Participants can post attachments through a frontend forum form. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

The Simply Schedule Appointments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.13.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The stored payload is only rendered when an administrator navigates to the hidden support page (/wp-admin/admin.php?ssa-support-admin=1) and triggers the 'Fix appointment durations' action, a condition reliably engineered by the attacker by smuggling a '+1 day' suffix in the start_date field to create a persistent duration mismatch that routes the malicious booking through the vulnerable echo path. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Paid Membership Plugin, Ecommerce, User Registration Form, Login Form, User Profile & Restrict Content – ProfilePress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'reg_bio' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The reg_bio parameter is accepted by the registration handler's allowlist even when the rendered registration form does not include a biography field, meaning an unauthenticated attacker can supply the payload via a raw POST request without needing a visible biography input on the form.
Tanium addressed a command injection vulnerability in Comply.

A flaw was found in D-Bus. With a privileged Monitoring client attached (for example dbus-monitor or busctl monitor), an unprivileged local user can cause dbus-daemon to abort if a driver-originated broadcast such as NameOwnerChanged or ActivatableServicesChanged cannot be delivered to a recipient (for example due to a deny rule or an exceeded outgoing message queue). Driver broadcasts still use serial 0; when delivery fails, composing the monitor error reply asserts reply_serial != 0 and aborts the daemon.
Incorrect authorization in Azure Managed Service Identity allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Improper certificate validation in Microsoft Office PowerPoint allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

A flaw was found in libslirp in if_output(). When moving a session from the fast queue to the batch queue, the code unlinked and reinserted an arbitrary packet via ifm->m_nextpkt instead of the session queue head, corrupting queue pointers. A guest generating burst traffic could crash the host networking process, causing a denial of service.

A format string vulnerability has been reported in the Internal Backup of ADM. User-controlled input from the source_folders parameter is passed by internalbackup.cgi to a shared string-copy routine in libbackup.so.0.0 and used directly as the format-string argument to snprintf() without corresponding variadic arguments. This may allow an authenticated attacker to disclose process memory addresses or trigger unintended memory writes that terminate the affected CGI process.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability in the ADM Notifications allows network eavesdroppers on the outbound network path to obtain Clickatell service credentials via the SMS. When executing an SMS test for Clickatell Communicator Central, the backend function Send_Test_SMS embeds the sensitive contents directly into an unencrypted HTTP request URL. An observer on the NAS network egress path can capture the plain text credentials and message payload since the initial request is transmitted without TLS protection or secret redaction.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An External Control of File Name or Path (Argument Injection) vulnerability in the settings/notification.cgi component of ADM allows authenticated remote administrators to create or truncate arbitrary files with root privileges via crafted request parameters. An authenticated administrator can truncate arbitrary critical files across the root filesystem, leading to system failure or Denial of Service (DoS).
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An argument injection vulnerability exists in the settings/vpn.cgi endpoint in the ADM. When processing a WireGuard profile, the internal command parser removes quotes and performs a quote-agnostic scan on arguments without properly sanitizing redirection operators. An authenticated administrator can supply a crafted parameter to cause the execution helper to open and truncate arbitrary files on the filesystem with root privileges, resulting in an arbitrary file truncation and denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An arbitrary file creation and truncation vulnerability exists in the File Explorer of ADM. An authenticated low-privileged user can upload a file with crafted path components containing quote and redirection characters. When music.cgi processes the entry for audio playback operations, the unescaped path string breaks out of the expected argument context in the internal command parser. This causes the system execution helper to open the attacker-specified path with root privileges using O_TRUNC, allowing remote attackers to truncate or create arbitrary system files.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the initialization component of ADM. When the NAS is uninitialized, the endpoint accepts an unauthenticated sid query parameter and inserts its URL-decoded value into an inline JavaScript string without proper JavaScript-context encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when opened by a user, executes arbitrary JavaScript in the ADM management origin. Successful exploitation may allow manipulation of the setup page and execution of same-origin requests in the victim's browser. The vulnerability is limited to the first-run initialization state.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Insufficient bounds checks in the Link Aggregation handler of ASUSTOR ADM allow an authenticated administrator to submit an excessive number of interface tokens. Crafted requests can corrupt memory and terminate the affected privileged CGI process.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Wi-Fi connection handler of ADM allows an authenticated administrator to corrupt heap memory and terminate the affected CGI request by supplying an oversized Wi-Fi pre-shared key.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A stack-based buffer overflow in the DHCP Server helper of ASUSTOR ADM allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to trigger stack memory corruption by sending a crafted DHCP hostname to a device with DHCP Server enabled. This may disrupt DHCP service.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper certificate validation vulnerability exists in ADM App Central, due to disabled peer verification within the set-used-server endpoint, enabling an unauthenticated Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacker to intercept HTTPS traffic, bypass TLS validation, and modify App Central server redirection settings to cause a persistent service outage for application updates without bypassing package signature verification.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A path traversal vulnerability in the regional options of ADM allows attackers to read arbitrary files on the system. The function fails to properly canonicalize user-supplied directory paths, enabling attackers to bypass path restriction checks via crafted path traversal sequences.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper TLS certificate validation vulnerability exists in the ADM online update service. An unauthenticated attacker capable of performing a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack against the device's firmware update connection can impersonate the update server using an untrusted TLS certificate and supply malicious update metadata. The attacker may cause a crafted firmware image to be installed and execute arbitrary code with root privileges when automatic firmware updates are enabled.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the ADM allows remote authenticated administrators to cause a denial of service (service crash) or potentially execute arbitrary code via a crafted tag parameter in settings CGI.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A relative path traversal vulnerability in the FTP Backup of ADM, allows an attacker controlling a configured FTP server to cause files to be created or overwritten outside the selected NAS backup destination. Successful exploitation can modify or destroy files writable by that identity.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An OS command injection vulnerability in ADM allows remote authenticated administrators to execute arbitrary commands as root. The set action in settings/ddns.cgi fails to sanitize configuration delimiters in user-supplied parameters before writing them into the DDNS configuration file, allowing an attacker to inject directives that execute arbitrary system commands upon service restart.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A potential stack-based buffer overflow exists in ADM Defender Firewall configuration handling. Before the fix, firewall policy processing used string operations without sufficient destination-size checks and did not consistently validate array bounds. Malformed or oversized configuration data may cause an out-of-bounds write and corrupt stack memory.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An OS command injection vulnerability in the PPPoE configuration of ADM allows an authenticated administrator to store shell syntax in the PPPoE account value. When the service loads the resulting configuration, the injected commands can execute with root privileges.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the wallpaper component of ADM. An authenticated, low-privileged user can bypass shared-folder access controls by specifying an image path within a restricted share. The CGI processes the request with root privileges without enforcing the source share's access permissions, allowing the attacker to copy and retrieve images they are not authorized to access, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the IP block management component of ADM due to insufficient input validation and bounds checking. This vulnerability may allow an authenticated administrator to cause memory corruption, potentially resulting in application crashes or denial of service (DoS).
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An externally-controlled format string vulnerability exists in the authenticated upload_wireguard action of settings/vpnupload.cgi in the ADM. The CGI takes an attacker-controlled WireGuard profile name, inserts it into a JSON object, serializes it, and passes the resulting formatted string directly to printf as the format argument without validation or escaping. An authenticated remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending format string specifiers, or leverage variadic read/write primitives within the non-PIE, non-Canary root CGI to potentially achieve arbitrary remote code execution with root privileges.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

The affected products insufficiently restrict runtime-supplied visualization data, allowing local program execution on the engineering workstation, if a user is both logged in to a CODESYS Control runtime and operates a visualization. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious runtime and tricking a user to trust it, or performing a man-in-the-middle attack on the communication between the CODESYS Control runtime and the engineering workstation, may cause arbitrary code execution on the engineering workstation.

The affected products insufficiently restrict runtime-supplied visualization data, allowing to invoke local COM/ActiveX functionality on the engineering workstation, if a user is both logged in to a CODESYS Control runtime and operates a visualization. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious runtime and tricking a user to trust it, or performing a man-in-the-middle attack on the communication between the CODESYS Control runtime and the engineering workstation, may cause arbitrary code execution on the engineering workstation.

The affected products insufficiently restrict runtime-supplied visualization commands, allowing local functionality on the engineering workstation to be invoked, if a user is both logged in to a CODESYS Control runtime and operates a visualization. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious runtime and tricking a user to trust it, or performing a man-in-the-middle attack on the communication between the CODESYS Control runtime and the engineering workstation, may cause arbitrary code execution on the engineering workstation.

An unauthenticated attacker can trick a local user into generating an offline boot application from a malicious CODESYS project, causing the affected products to write files in arbitrary directories on the engineering workstation. The destination path is derived from attacker-controlled project data, whereas the file name and file contents are generated by the affected products and are not attacker-controlled.

A flaw was found in the GStreamer JPEG 2000 decimator in gst-plugins-bad. Crafted JPEG 2000 media can cause integer overflows or division by zero during tile processing. An application that processes the malicious media may crash, resulting in a denial of service.

InDesign Desktop is affected by a Divide By Zero vulnerability that could result in an application denial-of-service. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to crash the application, leading to a denial-of-service condition. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must open a malicious file.

Reflected cross-site scripting in the versioned REST API documentation page in Checkmk versions 2.5.0 before 2.5.0p21 allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of a user who opens a crafted link, in the context of that user's Checkmk session. The API version segment of the documentation URL is inserted into the page without escaping, and the page is reachable without authentication.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in the Axivion Suite ApiToken permission restriction for OIDC and SAML users of the Axivion Dashboard. 
When a user creates an ApiToken with a restricted token type (for example, IDE plugin or Continuous Integration), some of that user’s permissions should be removed from the token. For users who sign in to the Dashboard through OIDC, or through the SAML preview feature, this restriction has no effect. Exploitability is low: an attacker needs an ApiToken that has been leaked, or one that was shared on the assumption that its permissions were restricted.

Insufficient authorization in personal notification rules in Checkmk <2.5.0p20, <2.4.0p41 and 2.3.0 (EOL) allows authenticated users to receive notifications for hosts and services they are not a contact of by defining broad personal notification rules.

Issue summary: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData
message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with
the square of the message size.

Impact summary: An attacker who can submit a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message
to an application that verifies it with CRL checking enabled can occupy a CPU
core for seconds to minutes, causing Denial of Service. Applications that
leave CRL checking disabled are not affected.

CWE: CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity

Description: With CRL checking enabled, OpenSSL compares each CRL distribution
point of a certificate against the issuing distribution point of every
candidate CRL. For a nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution point, the full name
is the CRL issuer name with the relative name appended. Since the change that
deferred this computation, crl_crldp_check() rebuilds that full name for each
candidate CRL and frees it again.

CMS_verify() and PKCS7_verify() take both the distribution points and the
candidate CRLs from the message, and this scoring runs before any signature is
checked. An application is exposed only if it sets X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK on
the store and does not pass CMS_NOCRL or PKCS7_NOCRL; CRL checking is off by
default. In TLS the CRLs come from the local store, so a peer controls only
the distribution point count.

The cost grows with the product of the distribution point count, the CRL count
and the issuer name length, all chosen by the message author; a few hundred
kilobytes can occupy a CPU core for tens of seconds. Verification still fails
as it should, with no crash, no incorrect result and no memory growth.
Requiring CRL checking is what limits the severity.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's MXF demuxer plugin (gst-plugins-bad). When processing a specially crafted MXF media file, the demuxer indexes its internal delta-entry and slice-offset tables using values from the file without validating that they are within the bounds of the allocated arrays. A local attacker who tricks a user into opening a malicious MXF file can cause the application to crash (denial of service) and may be able to read limited amounts of heap memory adjacent to the affected arrays.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-bad package. A use of uninitialized memory vulnerability exists in the H.265 (HEVC) bitstream parser when processing Video Parameter Sets that declare more than one HRD (Hypothetical Reference Decoder) parameter set. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a crafted H.265 media file or stream that, when processed by an application using GStreamer, causes unpredictable parser behavior and may crash the application. This can lead to a denial of service for any application using GStreamer to play back H.265 content.

RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. In the affected revision identified by the advisory, the AMQP 1.0 server_mode parser in deps/amqp10_common/src/amqp10_binary_parser.erl stops at the first body section and preserves the remaining bytes in bare_and_footer without validating message-section order. An authenticated publisher with write permission can place a properties section carrying a forged user-id after the body, causing rabbit_access_control:check_user_id/2 to see no user-id while permissive downstream AMQP 1.0 decoders or AMQP 0-9-1 conversion through classic and quorum queues expose the forged identity. Applications that rely on RabbitMQ-validated user-id metadata can therefore accept attacker-controlled publisher attribution. Strict consumers that reject out-of-order sections are not vulnerable to identity spoofing, and the issue does not bypass broker routing or destination authorization. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.5.

Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input in the GNU C Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

A flaw was found in Podman. An attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a container image containing crafted metadata labels. Podman's auto-update mechanism improperly trusts these image labels to determine which system services to restart. If a user runs the malicious container and auto-update processes it, arbitrary system services are restarted with the user's privileges, potentially allowing an attacker to shut down the host system when Podman runs with administrative privileges.

A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. A heap-based buffer overflow can occur when processing a specially crafted Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) document using the sds-compose option. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt memory, resulting in an application crash and a Denial of Service (DoS).

Pelican 4.12.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in pelican-import. An attacker-controlled wp:post_name from a WordPress XML export is used in an output filename that is interpolated into a Pandoc command passed to subprocess.call with shell=True. On POSIX systems, command substitution in the slug is evaluated when a user imports the crafted export.

The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'section_title_tag' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Although the plugin ships a resolveSectionTitleTag() helper that enforces an [h1–h6, p] allow-list, the accordion render path never invokes it, and the wp_kses_post sanitization applied to post_content on save does not parse shortcode attribute text, leaving the malicious value stored verbatim.

The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'values[text_shadow_color]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post sanitization applied at save time does not strip the payload because it is stored as URL-encoded JSON inside a shortcode attribute, containing no literal HTML tags for kses to tokenize, leaving the malicious value intact until render time.

A flaw was found in the ansible-core user module. When generate_ssh_key is enabled, User.ssh_key_gen() guards the key files against symlinks but checks the ~/.ssh directory only with os.path.exists(). An unprivileged user on a managed node who replaces their ~/.ssh with a symlink to an existing root-writable directory causes the privileged module to write the generated key pair through the symlink and then chown both files to that user. Because such files can be dropped into directories processed by schedulers (e.g. /etc/cron.daily) or dynamic MOTD (/etc/update-motd.d), the user can escalate to root on the managed node. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2024-9902.

Multiple Farmasimplex healthcare integration modules do not properly validate TLS certificates, allowing an attacker who can intercept network traffic to impersonate trusted healthcare services and perform man-in-the-middle attacks, potentially leading to disclosure or modification of sensitive data.

The REV.exe module distributed with Farmasimplex contains embedded OAuth client credentials for integration with the IZS platform. An attacker with access to the executable could extract and reuse the credentials, potentially leading to unauthorized access to integration resources or manipulation of associated information, depending on the privileges granted and authentication controls in place.

The CeliachiaRL integration component distributed with Farmasimplex uses shared OAuth credentials across multiple customer installations. An attacker who obtains the credentials from one installation could reuse them against services associated with other installations, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information or modification of integration data.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by an Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user. A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.
Incorrect authorization in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

An unauthenticated attacker could trigger an Out of Memory condition to crash the Java process for RHCS by repeatedly sending HTTP requests to the TLS endpoint. Depending on how the RHCS server is configured, a manual intervention to restart it may prove necessary.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. An unauthenticated client can obtain an anonymous registry token with an audience it controls, present that token to the service key rotation endpoint, and install its own approved signing key with no expiry. Registry tokens signed with that key are accepted for any repository, allowing read and write access to private images and replacement of repository tags.

A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

A flaw was found in the default seccomp profile used by Podman via containers-common. Deny rules for AF_VSOCK and NETLINK_AUDIT compared socket arguments with unmasked 64-bit equality. Because the kernel truncates those int arguments to 32 bits, setting upper bits can bypass the deny rules.

Spring Data Elasticsearch replaces positional placeholders in string-based @Query methods with the method arguments before it evaluates SpEL expressions in the resulting query string.



As a result, an argument that contains a SpEL expression is evaluated as part of the query, even if the declared query does not use SpEL.



 An application is affected if it passes untrusted input as an argument to a repository query method that declares a @Query with positional placeholders.



In that case, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary code in the application, and repeated requests can exhaust memory through the unbounded expression cache.

The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'thread[body]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution of the injected script is limited to viewers whose forum access profile denies attachment viewing (va=0 or caa=0), meaning exploitation depends on an administrator having configured a custom forum access profile that permits reading but denies attachment viewing — this is not the default shipped configuration.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a mass assignment vulnerability in the patient portal OnsiteDocument query API that lets request parameters set bitwise criteria filters whose values are placed unquoted into the SQL WHERE clause. Authenticated patient portal users can inject SQL via parameters such as Id_BitwiseAnd to read any database table, including other patients' records and staff password hashes.

OpenEMR from 7.0.1 before 8.4.0 contains a flaw in src/Common/Auth/OneTimeAuth.php that ignores the enforce_onetime_use and max_access_count flags, never revokes consumed service_auth tokens, and checks login_pin without rate limiting or strict comparison. Attackers holding a captured token can replay it or brute-force the PIN to open patient-portal sessions exposing PHI.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the FaxSMS module's RCFaxClient and SignalWireClient disposeDocument functions that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read and overwrite arbitrary files via the unsanitized file_path parameter. Attackers can request action=download to retrieve cleartext files like sqlconf.php database credentials and keys, or use action=setup to overwrite web-server-writable files with ciphertext.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsitePortalActivityController::Update() that checks the request's patientId instead of the stored record's owner. Authenticated portal patients can send PUT requests to the onsiteportalactivity API with another patient's activity id and their own patientId to disclose tableArgs and checksum data, overwrite narratives and status, and take ownership of the record.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the CCDA/CCD preview stylesheets, where cda.xsl copies event-handler attributes whose values evade a character denylist and ccd.xsl copies table-cell attributes unsanitized into preview HTML. Authenticated users can upload a crafted CCDA/CCD document with onmouseover, onclick, or onfocus handlers to execute script in a clinician's session when previewed.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in FHIR Media/:uuid and QuestionnaireResponse read routes that skip ACL checks. Non-patient API tokens lacking OpenEMR ACLs can request resources by uuid, bypassing compartment filtering to read any patient's documents and questionnaire responses.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a broken access control and path traversal vulnerability in the fax/sms module disposeDocument action via an unvalidated file_path parameter. Authenticated low-privilege users can read sqlconf.php to recover database credentials and write arbitrary files as the web user, enabling remote code execution.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its SMART on FHIR implementation because checkUserHasAccessToPatient() in BearerTokenAuthorizationStrategy.php unconditionally returns true. Authenticated users or malicious SMART apps can manipulate token launch context to bind requests to arbitrary patient UUIDs, gaining unauthorized read/write access to other patients' FHIR resources.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in interface/forms/eye_mag/report.php that allows authenticated users to inject scripts by adding unescaped document notes. Attackers with document-note write access can store malicious JavaScript in a retina document note that executes when clinicians generate the Eye Exam patient report, exposing session cookies.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in portal/lib/persist.php that allows authenticated portal patients to write settings for other patients. Attackers can modify the setting_patient parameter in a JSON POST request to another patient's PID, altering that patient's portal settings such as the portal theme.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsiteDocumentController::Query() that allows authenticated portal patients to read other patients' documents by overriding Pid_Equals criteria. Attackers can supply Pid_Equals, Pid_GreaterThan, or Pid_In request parameters to the onsitedocuments API to retrieve signed consent forms, signatures, and PHI of any patient.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains missing authorization and insecure direct object reference vulnerabilities in the oe-module-prior-authorizations module that allow authenticated low-privilege users to access and modify other patients' records. Attackers can request public/reports/list_report.php to view all patients' names, MRNs, insurance and prior-auth data, or submit arbitrary id values to public/index.php to overwrite other patients' prior-authorization records.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in interface/billing/sl_eob_process.php that allows authenticated users to write and read files by supplying unsanitized eraname values. Attackers without billing privileges can inject ../ sequences to create ERA report .html files anywhere the web user can write and parse arbitrary .edi files echoed into the report.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the FHIR GET /fhir/Person/:uuid route that allows patient-portal users to read any staff member's demographics by bypassing compartment enforcement. Attackers holding a patient SMART token with patient/Person.read can harvest staff Person UUIDs from Appointment references to retrieve names, home addresses, phone numbers, and personal emails.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in many encounter-form view and save endpoints that lack patient/encounter ownership checks. Authenticated clinical users can enumerate sequential form id values in requests such as soap/view.php and save.php to read and overwrite other patients' clinical records.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in PortalPatientController::Read() that allows authenticated patients to read other patients' pending demographic change requests. Attackers can supply another patient's ID in the patientId query string parameter to retrieve PHI including names, addresses, SSNs, and insurance information.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD server. A remote attacker can crash a multi-export NBD server process by exploiting stale metadata export state during an extended BLOCK_STATUS request, resulting in an assertion failure and denial of service.

The shell command ACL for the feature scope (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg) restricts feature:install, feature:uninstall, feature:start and feature:stop to the admin role, but had no entry for feature:requirement-add or feature:requirement-remove.

The provisioning resolver turns a requirement into the same install/start (or uninstall) action as feature:install / feature:uninstall: a bundle: requirement causes an arbitrary bundle to be downloaded and started, and a feature: requirement installs that feature. Because the two commands had no ACL, a user authenticated with only the viewer (and ssh) role could invoke them and cause Apache Karaf to download, install and start an attacker-chosen bundle, which then runs with the full authority of the Karaf process — thereby bypassing the admin-only authorization enforced on feature:install and bundle:install.

This is the same class of issue as the feature:repo-add -i / feature:repo-remove -u bypass, on sibling commands not covered by that earlier fix.Mitigation:Upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.12 or 4.5.0 (or later), which restrict feature:requirement-add and feature:requirement-remove to the admin role.

As an interim workaround on affected versions, add the following two lines to etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg; the change is picked up at runtime without a restart:

requirement-add = admin

requirement-remove = admin

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.9, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware with a matcher that requires a non-empty value for a dynamic segment, while Fastify's router accepts an empty parameter or wildcard value. When a route and an Express middleware mount share a dynamic pattern, a request with an empty segment matches the Fastify route and runs the handler while the middleware mounted on that pattern is skipped, so on a scoped mount an unauthenticated request can reach a protected handler. No special configuration is required, and the practical impact depends on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

The fix for CVE-2026-0716 (commit 6ff7ef0, libsoup 3.6.6) placed the integer overflow guard inside the if (masked) block, leaving unmasked server-to-client frames unprotected. A malicious WebSocket server can send a crafted unmasked frame with a payload length near UINT64_MAX to trigger an OOB read in a libsoup-based client when max_incoming_payload_size is set to 0.

Authorization bypass using a user-controlled token (IDOR) on the GlobalEduca job portal. The GET endpoint ‘/attachments/{attachment_id}’ fails to verify whether the attachment belongs to the authenticated user. A user with a registered account can enumerate sequential identifiers and download attachments belonging to other candidates, including resumes containing personal data.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'carta_presentacion[contenido]' field in the POST request to '/personas/{persona_id}/cvs/{cv_id}/carta_presentaciones' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

Uploading PDF files with active content to the languages form. The POST endpoint ‘/people/{person_id}/languages’ checks the declared MIME type and allows an authenticated user to upload a PDF with embedded JavaScript. The portal serves the file via a GET request to ‘/attachments/{attachment_id}’ with the ‘Content-Disposition: inline’ header, so it can be opened in the browser’s PDF viewer during review. The handling of active content depends on the viewer used.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'experiencia_laboral[descripcion]' field in the POST request to '/personas/{persona_id}/experiencias_laborales' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'activity[description]' field in the POST request to '/people/{person_id}/cvs/{cv_id}/activities' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

An information disclosure vulnerability in Zstandard versions 1.5.1 through 1.5.7 allows specially crafted compressed data to expose the contents of an internal buffer through decompressed output. The buffer is 64 KiB in the default configuration and may contain uninitialized memory or literals from earlier decompressions performed using the same decompression context. An attacker who can submit compressed data and observe the resulting output can recover the buffer's contents.

The Swift Performance Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<attacker-chosen parameter name>' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.7.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that an administrator has configured at least one Cacheable AJAX Action via the plugin's AJAX Cache feature, a condition attackers can confirm by probing for a swift-performance: HIT response header.

The EZ SQL Reports Shortcode Widget and DB Backup plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'User-Agent header (stored to comment_agent)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.26.45 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has saved a report whose SQL query selects attacker-controlled data such as comment_agent, and that the attacker can identify the saved report's slug — a condition trivially met when the administrator publishes the report on a public page via the [SQLREPORT] shortcode.

A flaw was found in the SRT and WebVTT subtitle parser in GStreamer's gst-plugins-base. While sanitizing inline subtitle markup, the parser repeatedly searches the remaining text with unanchored regular expressions. A crafted subtitle cue with a long line of unmatched markup-like text can force quadratic CPU use and make a GStreamer-based application unresponsive.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-good MOV/MP4 demuxer. When processing an uncompressed video track, qtdemux fails to validate the declared row alignment and chroma geometry before using them to build a video buffer layout. A crafted file can cause an out-of-bounds heap read while the sample is copied, potentially crashing the application and causing denial of service.

The administration page "Offene
Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the
customer name of pending orders without output encoding. A registered
customer (free self-registration) can submit an HTML-entity-encoded name, which is
decoded to markup when the billing address of an order is written. If
the PayPal payment is left unfinished, the order is listed on the page and the
name is rendered as markup in the browser of an administrator who opens
the page. The script code runs with the privileges of that administrator
and can, for example, create a new administrator account. Guest orders are
not affected, because the name is encoded again.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Motion Pixels decoder because mp_decode_frame() ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers supplying a roughly 2^28-byte packet through the libavcodec API overflow the bit count, causing reads from a NULL buffer that crash the process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in tqi_decode_frame() in libavcodec/eatqi.c, which ignores init_get_bits() failure after an integer overflow. Attackers can supply a crafted EA file with a pIQT chunk carrying a 2^28-byte payload to crash the process, causing denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in libavcodec/jvdec.c that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying oversized JV video packets. Attackers can pass a roughly 268435460-byte packet through the libavcodec API, overflowing the bit count so decode_frame() reads from a NULL buffer and causes denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in mp_decode_frame() in libavcodec/mpegaudiodec_template.c because init_get_bits() failure is ignored after a signed integer overflow. Attackers can pass an oversized packet to the mp3adu decoder through the libavcodec API, causing reads through a NULL buffer that crash the process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in bit_allocation() in libavcodec/imc.c that allows attackers to hang decoding by supplying audio blocks with a negative bit budget. Attackers can craft IMC or IAC audio files that drive freebits negative, causing the reduction loop to never terminate and consuming 100% CPU.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory use vulnerability in the C93 video decoder in libavcodec/c93.c, where decode_frame() never checks how many color table bytes were copied. Attackers can supply a crafted truncated Interplay C93 file so draw_n_color() writes uninitialized stack bytes into decoded frames, disclosing stack memory contents.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in libavcodec/tiertexseqv.c that allows attackers to leak stack contents by triggering failed RLE unpacking. Attackers can supply a crafted Tiertex SEQ file so seq_decode_op1() copies an uninitialized 64-byte stack block into decoded frames, exposing stack memory in visible output.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in raw_decode() in libavcodec/rawdec.c that fails to verify packet stride covers a full row for 1 to 8 bits per pixel video. Attackers can supply crafted AVI, MOV or NUT files with truncated low bit depth rawvideo packets to leak uninitialized heap memory through decoded frame output.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in vp8_lossy_decode_alpha() in libavcodec/webp.c that leaves alpha plane memory uninitialized for short uncompressed ALPH chunks. Attackers can supply a crafted WebP image whose ALPH chunk is shorter than width * height to disclose stale pixel data from previously decoded frames.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in the GEM raster image decoder in libavcodec/gemdec.c that exposes uninitialized row-buffer bytes. Attackers can supply a crafted GEM .img image using SKIP or pattern opcodes to copy uninitialized heap memory into decoded frames, disclosing heap contents.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the OpenEXR decoder's decode_frame() in libavcodec/exr.c that miscalculates the tiled block count. Attackers can supply a crafted tiled OpenEXR image with large dimensions and small tiles to skip decoding and disclose uninitialized memory or stale frame data.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the VMnc decoder in libavcodec/vmnc.c that restores an unwritten cursor save area into later frames. Attackers can supply a crafted VMnc stream where a frame fails after loading a cursor shape, causing uninitialized heap bytes from screendta to appear in decoded output.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in tak_decode_frame() in libavcodec/takdec.c that fails to verify multichannel decorrelation lists cover every channel. Attackers can supply crafted multichannel TAK files omitting channels from the list, causing undecoded sample buffers to leak heap memory through decoded audio.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in flashsv_decode_block() in libavcodec/flashsv.c that copies uninitialized heap memory into decoded frames when inflate output is short. Attackers can supply a crafted FLV with an FSV1 stream whose zlib block data decompresses short, then recover heap contents from the decoded or re-encoded output.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory read vulnerability in decode_hybrid() in libavcodec/flashsv.c that reads past decompressed data when decoding 15-bit color pixels. Attackers can supply a crafted Flash Screen Video 2 block whose inflated data ends mid-pixel to leak heap memory into decoded output frames.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MSCC/SRGC decoder in libavcodec/mscc.c that outputs uninitialized heap bytes when RLE data ends early. Attackers can craft an MSCC or SRGC stream, such as in AVI, whose RLE data terminates early so the decoded frame exposes leftover heap memory to viewers of the output.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds heap read vulnerability in tdsc_load_cursor() in libavcodec/tdsc.c, which stores cursor dimensions before validating them. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI file with oversized TDSC cursor dimensions so tdsc_paint_cursor() reads past the cursor buffer, crashing the decoder or leaking heap memory into frames.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in the VQA video decoder in libavcodec/vqavideo.c that allows attackers to disclose heap memory via a crafted VQA file. Attackers can supply a Westwood VQA file omitting or truncating the CBF0/CBFZ codebook chunk, causing vqa_decode_frame() to render frames from leftover heap bytes visible in decoded output.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Arraytics WP Event Solution wp-event-solution allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Event Solution: from n/a through 4.1.30.

A heap out-of-bounds read flaw was found in libsoup. When parsing multipart HTTP messages, an integer type mismatch between the caller and soup_headers_parse() can cause the length parameter to be incorrectly truncated, leading to a heap buffer over-read. A remote attacker could use this flaw to crash an application using libsoup or potentially disclose heap memory contents.

The fix for CVE-2026-2443 was regressed by a subsequent rework commit that replaced specific overflow checks with a general signed comparison. When a client sends a Range request with a suffix length exceeding the content size, the resulting negative start value is not properly clamped, leading to malformed HTTP 206 responses and log flooding.

Cleartext storage in encrypted parquet file vulnerability in Apache Arrow Rust (`parquet` crate), from version 55.0.0 through to 57.3.2, 58.4.1, 59.3.2 and 60.1.0.



When writing an encrypted parquet file with a column with bloom filters, the header and bitsets of the bloom filter are written in plaintext in the final parquet.



Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 57.3.3, 58.4.2, 59.3.3 or 60.2.0 which fix the issue by raising an error when trying to write encrypted parquet files with bloom filters enabled, preventing such files from being written out.



Existing encrypted parquet files written with bloom filters are still vulnerable, and it is recommended to rewrite those files with bloom filters disabled if possible.

A flaw was found in cockpit-storaged. A Tang keyserver address read from a clevis token in a LUKS header is concatenated into curl's argument vector without a "--" separator. An address beginning with "-" is parsed by curl as an option instead of a hostname, allowing an attacker who can attach a crafted LUKS/clevis block device (for example, a local unprivileged user with an active console or desktop login session) to have an administratively-privileged Cockpit user unknowingly trigger curl option injection when editing the device's Tang keyserver settings. This can lead to arbitrary file read or write as the Cockpit session user.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD server. A remote attacker can crash qemu-nbd, qemu-storage-daemon, or qemu-system by sending NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT or NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT with a declared option length exceeding the actual payload, triggering an assertion failure and denial of service.

A flaw was found in the GStreamer gst-plugins-bad MXF plugin. Insufficient bounds checks when parsing crafted VANC data can cause an out-of-bounds read in the demuxer, while an incorrect buffer size calculation when muxing multiple ancillary packets can cause an out-of-bounds write. Processing affected content may crash the application, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-bad MPEG Program Stream demuxer and resindvd DVD-playback plugin. The PES header parsers do not adequately check remaining data before reading timestamps and optional header fields. Opening a specially crafted MPEG Program Stream file can cause an out-of-bounds read and potentially crash the application, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by a reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to inject malicious scripts into a web page, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must visit a maliciously crafted URL or interact with a compromised web page. Scope is changed.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability that could result in privilege escalation. A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to gain elevated access to sensitive data or functionality. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) is affected by an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability that could result in a Security feature bypass. A low-privileged attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass security measures and gain unauthorized read and limited write access. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

SQL injection in the CabinPaq manual code entry module, versions v.1.2.94 and v.1.2.136. The application constructs SQL queries from terminal input without properly sanitising it. With physical access to the terminal, an attacker could bypass code validation and open compartments without authorisation.

A flaw was found in sssd. When authenticating with a YubiKey, the SSSD PAM responder can crash due to a use-after-free vulnerability, where a memory pointer is incorrectly handled. A local attacker could exploit this flaw by manipulating smartcard or YubiKey contents, leading to a denial of service that disrupts authentication. This vulnerability also presents a potential for privilege escalation, although it is difficult to exploit.

A improper neutralization of special elements used in a template engine vulnerability in Fortinet FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11 may allow a low privileged Device Manager admin to obtain super admin privilege on managed FortiGates via injecting malicious commands.

A improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.2 all versions, FortiManager 8.0.0, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 7.2 all versions may allow an authenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via a crafted HTTP request.

A improper certificate validation vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.13, FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiManager Cloud 8.0.1, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.13 may allow a MITM attacker to impersonate the radius server via a rogue RADIUS server.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.13, FortiOS 7.2 all versions may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or command via crafted packets.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1 through 24.2.00.

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Server Side Request Forgery.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1.01 Cum 03 through 12.1.01 Cum 06, from 24.0 through 24.2.00.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Collect Data from Common Resource Locations.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1.00 through 24.2.00.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File, Insufficiently Protected Credentials vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Reusing Session IDs (Session Replay).This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1.00 through 24.2.00.

Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Session Credential Falsification through Forging.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1 through 24.2.00.

Missing Authentication for Critical Function, OS Command Injection vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows OS Command Injection.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1 through 24.0.01.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Object Injection.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1 through 24.0.01.

Missing Authorization, Hidden Functionality vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs, Exploit Non-Production Interfaces.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1.00 through 24.2.00.

Invocation of Process Using Visible Sensitive Information, Insufficiently Protected Credentials vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (AutoSys engine (AE) native clients modules) on Windows, Linux allows Collect Data from Common Resource Locations.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: 24.2.00-0210 and earlier (verified on 24.2.00-0210; earlier range unestablished), 24.2.01 (when the -pw/-pwx options are used).

Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (AutoSys engine (AE) native clients modules) on Windows, Linux allows Overflow Buffers.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1.00.00-0305 through 24.2.00-0210.

OS Command Injection, Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows OS Command Injection, Command Delimiters.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1 through 24.2.00.

Missing authorization vulnerability in ASUS Control Center Datacenter and Control Center Enterprise allows remote authenticated users with a low-privileged Viewer role to change the password of an Administrator account, thereby obtaining administrative privileges, via a crafted password update request. 
Refer to the '
Security Update for ASUS Control Center  ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

Authentication bypass in the Face ID app lock in Proton Pass for iOS before v. 1.21.1 allows an attacker with physical access to an already unlocked device to open vault items behind the lock screen via VoiceOver, leading to the disclosure and modification of stored credentials.

A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. This vulnerability allows for information disclosure when performing offline scans of untrusted filesystem images, such as container images or virtual machine (VM) disks. Because the scanner does not properly restrict symbolic link (symlink) resolution to the target image's root directory, an attacker can supply a crafted image containing links pointing to files on the host system. When the scan runs, typically with elevated privileges, OpenSCAP follows these links to read sensitive host files and expose their contents in the scan report or manipulate compliance results.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD block driver. A malicious NBD server can send an incomplete structured read reply marked as done, causing QEMU to return uninitialized host heap memory to the guest VM, resulting in host memory disclosure.

Improper restriction of intended endpoints in the connection configuration handling of the AWS Labs Timestream for InfluxDB MCP Server (awslabs.timestream-for-influxdb-mcp-server) before 0.0.19 might allow a remote unauthenticated actor (via prompt injection) to obtain the InfluxDB API token configured on the server, sent to a crafted endpoint controlled through an InfluxDB URL introduced in the MCP client context.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.0.19 or later and rotate any InfluxDB API tokens configured for the server.

Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in the RDM folder duplication endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated low-privileged attacker to overwrite and move arbitrary vault entries and read their history via a client-supplied entry identifier.

Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in the cost report generation tool in AWS Pricing MCP Server (aws-pricing-mcp-server) before 1.0.31 might allow an actor who can influence the MCP agent to write actor controlled content to arbitrary locations outside the intended output directory via absolute paths or directory traversal sequences in the report output path.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 1.0.31 or later. Users of the deprecated awslabs.cost-analysis-mcp-server package should migrate to awslabs.aws-pricing-mcp-server version 1.0.31 or later.

A flaw was found in cpio. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering a stack-based buffer overflow when creating archives in tar or ustar formats. When archiving files owned by users or groups with names exceeding 32 characters, cpio copies these names into fixed-size memory without verifying their length. This unbounded copy corrupts stack memory and causes the application to crash.

The Foxtool All-in-One: Contact chat button, Custom login, Media optimize images WordPress plugin through 2.5.4 does not check that the current user owns or may delete a post's featured image before permanently deleting it along with the post, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to delete arbitrary image attachments from the media library, such as those uploaded by administrators, when the option to delete attached images on post deletion is enabled.

The 3D Website Builder WordPress plugin through 2.0.3 does not perform any authorisation check in one of its publicly accessible AJAX actions, and the nonce guarding it is exposed to visitors on any page embedding the 3D Website Builder WordPress plugin through 2.0.3's shortcode, allowing unauthenticated users to permanently delete any of the 3D Website Builder WordPress plugin through 2.0.3's 3D builder objects and their slides.
Rejected reason: This CVE ID has been rejected or withdrawn by its CVE Numbering Authority.

The
Danfoss legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 Series are vulnerable to unauthorized
access when default credentials or known passwords are used for authentication.
These products were manufactured with default credentials documented in the
product manual. All versions are affected.

A flaw was found in SSSD's conversion of X.509 certificate RSA public keys to SSH keys. Missing size checks before copying RSA components into fixed-size stack buffers can cause a stack buffer overflow. An attacker able to supply a certificate with oversized RSA components that passes the configured certificate checks can cause denial of service and corrupt SSH responder memory.

A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder on builds with the JSON PAM extension enabled. A local attacker can submit a crafted authentication request containing a non-string OAuth2 code value. Missing JSON type validation leads to a NULL pointer dereference, terminating the PAM responder and disrupting SSSD-backed authentication.

A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder. A local attacker can send an authentication request without first negotiating the client protocol version. The responder dereferences a NULL protocol-version pointer and crashes, disrupting SSSD-backed authentication. Repeated crafted requests can sustain the denial of service.
